title: Tailplane Attachment Fitting — Bore Corrosion and Fretting Refurbishment
abstract: Shop refurbishment of a tailplane attachment fitting showing fretting on the mating face or coating breakdown at the bore, with the blend limits, the re-protection scheme and the reassembly acceptance.

sections.purpose: This repair covers fretting on the attachment fitting mating faces and coating breakdown around the fitting bores, found at heavy maintenance with the stabiliser removed.
sections.damage_assessment: Clean the mating faces and the bore and examine under ten times magnification. Measure the fretting depth with the surface gauge at four positions across each mating face, and measure the coating loss area at each bore. The repair admits fretting up to 0.15 millimetres deep over an area not exceeding a quarter of the mating face, and coating loss over any area provided there is no measurable material loss at the bore. Any pitting deeper than 0.10 millimetres at the bore, or any bore diameter outside the drawing tolerance, is outside this repair and needs a repair approval request. Record the as-found condition photographically before any blending.
sections.repair_procedure: Blend the fretted area with the abrasive pad set, working across the fretting marks and keeping the blend inside the depth limit. Check the blended depth at four positions and confirm the face remains flat within the limit on the straight edge. Strip the coating from the bore land and remove all traces of the previous scheme. Apply the surface treatment and the wear coating to the current specification, respecting the cure schedule. Where the gusset is being replaced, fit the current item and the current anchor nut standard at the interface. Reassemble with new fasteners, torque to the value on the repair drawing and record the torque values. Apply the external protection scheme to the reassembled joint.
sections.inspection_requirements: Do a dye penetrant inspection of the blended mating face after blending and before coating, and record the result. Do a detailed visual inspection of the coating at every heavy check thereafter, with photographs against the scale card. Where the harder wear coating of the current specification has been applied, the visual inspection may be reduced to alternate heavy checks once two consecutive checks have shown no breakdown.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Fretting up to 0.15 mm deep over not more than a quarter of the mating face; coating loss with no measurable material loss at the bore; no pitting deeper than 0.10 mm.

repair_drawings.title: Attachment fitting mating face blend and bore re-protection

type_data.fastener_pattern: Existing fitting pattern retained; new fasteners at every position, torque as stated on the repair drawing
type_data.fatigue_life_note: No life limit when the blend stays inside the depth limit. Repeat visual inspection at every heavy check, reducible to alternate checks after two clear results with the current wear coating.
